{{Short description|Nonparametric test}}
In [[statistics]], the '''Brunner Munzel test'''<ref name="brunnerbook">{{cite book |last1=Brunner |first1=Edgar |last2=Bathke |first2=Arne |last3=Konietschke |first3=Frank |title=Rank and Pseudo-Rank Procedures for Independent Observations in Factorial Designs |date=2019 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-030-02912-8 |pages=137 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-02914-2 |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-030-02914-2 |language=en}}</ref><ref> {{cite journal |last1=Brunner |first1=E. |last2=Munzel |first2=U. |year=2000 |title=The nonparametric Behrens-Fisher problem: Asymptotic theory and a small-sample approximation |journal=Biometrical Journal |volume=42 |issue=1 |pages=17–25 |doi=10.1002/(SICI)1521-4036(200001)42:1<17::AID-BIMJ17>3.0.CO;2-U }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Neubert |first1=K. |last2=Brunner |first2=E. |year=2007 |title=A studentized permutation test for the non-parametric Behrens-Fisher problem |journal=Computational Statistics & Data Analysis |volume=51 |issue=10 |pages=5192–5204 |doi=10.1016/j.csda.2006.05.024 }}</ref>  (also called the '''generalized Wilcoxon test''') is a [[nonparametric statistics|nonparametric]] [[statistical hypothesis test|test]] of the [[null hypothesis]] that, for randomly selected values ''X'' and ''Y'' from two populations, the probability of ''X'' being greater than ''Y'' is equal to the probability of ''Y'' being greater than&nbsp;''X''. 

It is thus highly similar to the well-known [[Mann–Whitney U test]]. The core difference is that the Mann-Whitney U test assumes equal distributions under the null hypothesis  (see [[Mann–Whitney U test#Assumptions and formal statement of hypotheses]]), while the Brunner Munzel test does not require that assumption, making it more robust and applicable to a wider range of conditions. As a result, multiple authors recommend using the Brunner Munzel instead of the Mann-Whitney U test by default.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Karch |first1=J. D. |year=2021 |title=Psychologists should use Brunner-Munzel's instead of Mann-Whitney's U test as the default nonparametric procedure |journal=Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science |volume=4 |issue=2 |doi=10.1177/2515245921999602 |hdl=1887/3209569 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Noguchi |first1=K. |last2=Konietschke |first2=F. |last3=Marmolejo-Ramos |first3=F. |last4=Pauly |first4=M. |year=2021 |title=Permutation tests are robust and powerful at 0.5% and 5% significance levels |journal=Behavior Research Methods |volume=53 |issue=6 |pages=2712–2724 |doi=10.3758/s13428-021-01595-5 |doi-access=free |pmid=34050436 }}</ref>

==Assumptions and formal statement of hypotheses==

# All the observations from both groups are [[statistical independence|independent]] of each other,
# The responses are at least [[ordinal measurement|ordinal]] (i.e., one can at least say, of any two observations, which is the greater),
# Under the null hypothesis ''H''<sub>0</sub>, is that the probability of an observation from population ''X'' exceeding an observation from population ''Y'' is the same than the probability of an observation from ''Y'' exceeding an observation from ''X''; i.e.,  {{math|1=P(''X'' > ''Y'') = P(''Y'' > ''X'')}} or {{math|1=P(''X'' > ''Y'') + 0.5 · P(''X'' = ''Y'') = 0.5}}.
# The alternative hypothesis ''H''<sub>1</sub> is that {{math|1=P(''X'' > ''Y'') ≠ P(''Y'' > ''X'')}} or {{math|1=P(''X'' > ''Y'') + 0.5 · P(''X'' = ''Y'') ≠ 0.5}}

Under these assumptions, the test is consistent and approximately [[exact test|exact]].<ref name="brunnerbook"/> The crucial difference compared to the [[Mann–Whitney U test]] is that the latter is not approximately exact under these assumptions. Both tests are exact when additionally assuming equal distributions under the null hypothesis.

==Software implementations==
The Brunner Munzel test is available in the following packages
* [[R (programming language)|R]]: [https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/brunnermunzel/index.html {{mono|brunnermunzel}}], [https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lawstat/index.html {{mono|lawstat}}], [https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rankFD/index.html {{mono|rankFD}}] (function {{mono|rank.two.samples()}})
* [[Python (programming language)]]: [https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.brunnermunzel.html {{mono|scipy.stats.brunnermunzel}}]
* [[jamovi]]: [https://www.mdpi.com/2624-8611/5/2/26 {{mono|bmtest}}]
